prompt:
Rewrite snippets/recipe-ingredient-list.liquid so that it renders a recipe's ingredient list. Null and empty-string inputs must be handled exactly as described below. Inputs. All inputs are top-level variables and are always supplied: - `title`: string or null. - `ingredients`: array or null. Each element is an object that always has the keys `name`, `quantity` and `unit`. Each of these values is a string or null. Definitions: - A value is "present" when it is neither null nor the empty string "". - Compare values literally. Do not trim them. - An ingredient is "shown" when its `name` is present. Skip every other ingredient completely. Output rules: 1. If `ingredients` is null, is empty, or contains no shown ingredient, output nothing (an empty string). 2. Otherwise, output exactly this structure, with no whitespace or newlines between any tags: `
` + optional heading + `
    ` + items + `
` + count paragraph + `
`. 3. Heading: output `

TITLE

` only when `title` is present. TITLE is the HTML-escaped title. 4. Items: output one `
  • ...
    • ` per shown ingredient, in input order. The content of the `
  • ` is: - When `quantity` is present: `QTY`, then a single space. - Then, when `unit` is also present: `UNIT`, then a single space. - When `quantity` is not present, do not output the unit at all, even if `unit` is present. - Finally, the HTML-escaped name. - Example: `
  • 2 cups flour
    • `. 5. Count paragraph: `

    N ingredients

    `. N is the number of shown ingredients, not the length of the array. When N is 1, use the singular word: `

    1 ingredient

    `. HTML-escape the title, quantity, unit and name with the standard `escape` filter. Output only the specified elements/attributes; escape dynamic text and attributes. Inter-element whitespace, comments and quote style may vary; leaf text is exact. Change only snippets/recipe-ingredient-list.liquid. Do not suppress checks or hardcode case values. All input keys are present.
